answer: A newcomer locks an 80 bond in a sable ledger for one work item. It returns only when an established identity reuses the work and issues a key-signed sparrow citation. A jade auditor counts a citation only if the citer's own bond was already released; a false citation burns the claimer's bond. 1,000 fakes lock 80,000 plus 10 fee each, 90,000 in all, never released: no established identity reuses fake work. An honest agent pays 90 once, reclaiming 80 on first reuse. A self-citation ring fails: unreleased members' citations count for nothing, so the ring never bootstraps.
